stemMd:
**Text 1**
Uniform field methods allow researchers to compare observations from different sites. Without standardization, a difference in results might merely reflect a difference in procedure.

**Text 2**
A uniform procedure may interact differently with local conditions. The same trap, for instance, may be easier for an animal to detect in open ground than in dense vegetation. Standardization does not automatically equalize detectability.

Which statement best describes the relationship between the texts?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Text 2 proves that every standardized method is worthless.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Both texts reject comparisons across sites.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Text 1 argues that local conditions never differ.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Text 2 identifies a limitation of the comparability that Text 1 seeks through standardization.

explanationMd: Text 1 removes one source of difference by standardizing procedure. Text 2 notes another source—the interaction of procedure and setting—that can remain after standardization. The claims can be reconciled.

distractorRationale.c: It focuses on procedural differences without that universal claim.
distractorRationale.b: Both discuss how such comparisons should be interpreted.
distractorRationale.a: It questions automatic equivalence, not all usefulness.
